One host (WSL 3.0.3.0, Windows 10.0.26300.9711), networking mode nat only; mirrored/Consomme not measured.

Target = official Ubuntu 24.04.5 WSL image with a task-created uid-1000 default user (same uid as the controller user) instead of the image OOBE user; a root-default target and other distributions were not measured.

The controller is the owner's existing (not disposable) distribution; only client-side actions ran there. wsl.exe -l -v before and after the task compare equal (diff exit 0); the target was unregistered (exit 0).

Observed [O]: with the detached endpoint (agent_proxy + ssh-agent under setsid nohup, no session left) the target kept running for the whole watch (r1 120 s; r2 600 s; r3 without systemd 120 s), while the no-background-process controls stopped at the t+15 s poll with and without systemd. Reading [I]: idle shutdown does not end a running Mode B helper; the helper keeps the distribution running until something stops it, so the supervisor must stop it explicitly. Persistence beyond 600 s is [U].

The owner's .wslconfig idle settings (instanceIdleTimeout/vmIdleTimeout) were not read; the controls measure the effective baseline instead. documented_default_instanceIdleTimeout_ms is the documented default, not a measured value.
